epic.title: compat(renderer): preload runtime, sandboxed-preload require shim, process polyfill, disabled-<webview> contract, browser-quirk ledger
epic.body:
## Scope
`<webview>` tag (113 members, Tier 3) plus the renderer-side compat user-script: `ipcRenderer`/`contextBridge`/`webFrame` subset, `process` polyfill (`type='renderer'`, versions, argv from `additionalArguments`, platform/arch/env policy), `webUtils.getPathForFile`, preload execution order. Live today: macOS KEL-142 isolated `WKContentWorld` script + frozen page-world facade (`window.keld.invoke` only), main-frame-only, document start; no app-preload injection; no `@keld/web`.

## Corpus demand (corrected: draw.io DISABLES `<webview>` everywhere — all 7 hits are `webviewTag:false` or a `will-attach-webview` preventDefault)
draw.io preload: `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('electron', {request, registerMsgListener, sendMessage, listenOnce})` over `ipcRenderer.send/on/once`, `process.type/versions`, `--initial-adaptive-colors=` from `process.argv`, localStorage seeding, a Navigation-API guard. Zettlr preload: ipc {send, sendSync, invoke, on → off closure}, config get/set via sendSync, `process` {platform, version, versions, arch, uptime, getSystemVersion, env copy, argv}, `webUtils.getPathForFile`; `sandbox:false` on two windows that still only use the sandboxed allow-list.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: `webviewTag` accepted and defaulted false; `<webview>` is an unknown element; `will-attach-webview` registrable (never fires).
- L1: draw.io's preload runs byte-for-byte unmodified in a Keld content world and its page round trips work on macOS.
- L2: preload order (before page scripts), sandboxed `require` allow-list, process polyfill fields, isolation negative tests, Error/Symbol value-table semantics pass pinned entries per engine (✔ WK/WebKitGTK; ▲ WebView2 where no isolated world exists).
- L3: Zettlr preload (sync-returning wrappers) handled per the F04-A3/A5 decisions.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-142 (world/injection seam; spec revision for a third world and the relay), KEL-79 (WebView2 worlds, origin), KEL-80 (floor v2), KEL-132.

## Design facts fixed by research (invariants refuter; semantics refuter pending batch 2)
- Ship the renderer user-script + disabled-webview contract first; `<webview>` element stays Tier 3 as a host-owned child webview mapping (never a DOM-embedded engine), with zero corpus pressure.
- The preload runs in a dedicated app content world (third world) registered at document start on the same per-view user-content controller as the KEL-142 scripts, with a relay no broader than `window.keld.*`; the KEL-142 isolation negative tests must pass with the preload present (panel contested decision PANEL-D21 decides same-world vs third-world on measured results).
- `require('electron')` resolves exactly the sandboxed-preload module map (contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, webFrame, webUtils) plus events/timers/url and the globals Buffer/process/setImmediate/clearImmediate; preload bytes are host-loaded from the bundle-relative path inside the content-authenticated package (never an absolute path read).
- `process.env` re-exposure to the page (Zettlr) is an information-flow decision with no owner (open).
- Migrated apps change origin when `file://` or a custom scheme is replaced; web-storage continuity is a product decision (open F07-A6).

decision_tickets.title: Web-storage continuity when `keld migrate` replaces `file://`/custom-scheme origins: empty first launch (▲) or a one-shot host-side storage import?
decision_tickets.question: A migrated app changes origin, so localStorage/IndexedDB keyed to the old origin become invisible. Decide: declare "first launch under Keld starts with empty web storage" as a visibly labelled ▲ in the migrate report, or specify an engine-specific one-shot import (WK/WebView2/WebKitGTK data stores). draw.io stores `.configuration` and recents in localStorage.

decision_tickets.title: process.env re-exposure to the page (Zettlr copies process.env into the renderer) — information-flow policy
decision_tickets.question: On Keld the renderer has no process; the shim must synthesise `env`. Copying the host environment into the page leaks secrets; omitting it may break apps that read `process.env.NODE_ENV`. Decide the allow-list (e.g. NODE_ENV only) and the migrate report wording.

refuter_verdicts_batch1.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse: four uniques only; default-deny never bypassed; no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; no parallel process model/transport/schema/parser/policy owner; reuse of existing owners (KEL-75/76/77/78/79/80/53/74/102/135/139-144); measured performance claims; spec+Linear gate; prior decisions #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127 delegated direction. Note: the research object was truncated mid-F07-A3 (at alternatives_rejected); only F07-A1, F07-A2, F07-A3 were visible. Any later decision ids (e.g. F07-P1) were not received and are not judged.

verdicts.reason: The corpus facts survive (draw.io electron.js: webviewTag:false at 728/1090/1407/2210/3087, will-attach-webview preventDefault at 2223; Zettlr and quick-start have no <webview>), and keeping <webview> at Tier 3 matches arch 04 §4. But the 'ship now, as Tier-1 cells' set violates the author's own evidence and the spec+Linear gate in three ways. (1) It bundles sendSync, ipcRenderer.postMessage and webUtils.getPathForFile into the ship-now set while the same object marks sendSync as having no engine mechanism without the KEL-79 bulk lane (a prototype atom), getPathForFile as [unknown] on WebKit engines, and postMessage as owned by KEL-80 virtual ports (Backlog/High, narrowed to product-spine subsets by #322–#325). Those cannot be Tier-1 'ship now' cells; they are prototype/owner-gated. (2) Every renderer cell requires lifting the KEL-142 floor (channel 1 only, u16 channels, 4096 B, one pending; kel142 §4.1, macos_bridge.rs PAGE_FACADE_SCRIPT). kel142 §12 says any change to caller-selected identity, pending queue or envelope shape must 'stop and revise this spec'; wv_link.rs is 'deliberately not KIPC' and its envelope is a wire-protocol review gate. A1 lists blocked_by: [] — that is wrong. (3) arch 04 §4 Tier 1 names ipcMain/ipcRenderer/invoke and contextBridge; webUtils and a webFrame subset are not Tier-1 items (webFrame appears only in §3 layer 3 prose). The unknown about Zettlr's sandbox:false preloads is also resolvable now and was not: forge.config.js generateRendererEntrypoint gives every window the single preload source/common/modules/preload/index.ts, which imports only contextBridge/ipcRenderer/webUtils plus a type-only import, so sandbox:false is a ▲ (ignored with KELD-COMPAT diagnostic; preload needs no Node) rather than a ✘.

verdicts.correction: Split A1 into: (a) ship-after-spec Tier-1 cells with existing owners — webviewTag accepted/defaulted false, <webview> as HTMLUnknownElement, will-attach-webview registrable-never-fires (depends on the webContents facade owner, name it), contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld, ipcRenderer send/on/once/off/removeAllListeners/setMaxListeners/invoke, synthesized process subset; blocked_by: KEL-142 spec revision (string channels, multi-pending, host→renderer events, SCV codec via KEL-98), wire-protocol + public-API review gates, KEL-97/BrowserWindow owner; (b) prototype-gated: sendSync (KEL-79 scheme + sync XHR), postMessage (KEL-80), getPathForFile (per-engine feasibility). Record Zettlr sandbox:false as ▲-with-diagnostic, not ✘ or unknown. Drop webUtils/webFrame from the Tier-1 label; cite arch 04 §3 layer 3 for webFrame instead.

verdicts.reason: Engine placement facts survive: macOS install() uses one per-view WKUserContentController with the isolated script/handler in defaultClientWorld and only the frozen facade in pageWorld, AtDocumentStart, forMainFrameOnly=true, fail-closed below macOS 11 — appending preload+compat script there is the right seam. WebKitGTK APIs are correctly cited and, better than the author states, the UI process can both receive replies (register_script_message_handler_with_reply(name, world_name), 2.40) and evaluate into the named world (webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript(..., world_name, ...), 2.40), so the GTK [unknown] about needing a WebKitWebProcessExtension is resolved negative. Two load-bearing claims are false. (1) 'contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld = isolated→page proxy installed by the pageWorld facade pattern already used for window.keld': the existing pattern is an async window.postMessage relay whose shape KEL-142 §5.1 restricts to 'no broader shape than window.keld.invoke'; exposing arbitrary app function tables widens the relay grammar (§12: stop and revise), and an async relay cannot return values synchronously, which Zettlr's exposed config.get / citation callback require (they return sendSync results synchronously to the page). A cross-world synchronous call path (shared DOM per WKContentWorld doc, e.g. synchronous CustomEvent dispatch) is an unlisted design atom. (2) 'preload must contain no secrets or authority — which Keld's host-minted document nonce already guarantees' is wrong on WebView2: kel142 §5.2 step 4 has the isolated script retain the nonce outside the page world; with no isolated world on WebView2 the nonce would live in the page realm and be readable, so the identity model is not transferable. Identity there must come from host-side engine metadata: the ICoreWebView2 instance that raised WebMessageReceived (host-bound WebviewId) plus host-tracked navigation generation; WebMessageReceivedEventArgs.Source is only 'the URI of the document that sent this web message', not a frame identity. The 'self-gated to window === window.top' emulation is page-controlled and therefore not a boundary; whether ICoreWebView2.WebMessageReceived fires for child frames vs only ICoreWebView2Frame.WebMessageReceived was not verified by the author or by me.

verdicts.correction: Rewrite A2 as: macOS/Linux real isolation (✔) via the KEL-142 seam and WebKitGTK named worlds, with a new decision atom 'cross-world function proxy + synchronous return path' that requires a KEL-142 spec revision of the relay grammar (wire-protocol gate). For WebView2, state that the KEL-142 nonce model does not apply; the identity owner is the host-side COM event source (per-ICoreWebView2 WebviewId) plus host navigation generation, and the page-world script may hold nothing that authorizes. Replace 'self-gated to window.top' with a host-side rule: accept WebMessageReceived only from the ICoreWebView2 main-frame event, verify (cheapest experiment: a WebView2 fixture with a same-origin and a cross-origin iframe each calling window.chrome.webview.postMessage; record which host event fires). Keep blocked_by: KEL-142 revision, WebKitGTK direct-binding replacement of wry, KEL-79 CSP interaction.

verdicts.reason: The Electron contract mirror survives: sandbox.md names exactly contextBridge/crashReporter/ipcRenderer/nativeImage/webFrame/webUtils plus events/timers/url, 'you will not be able to use CommonJS modules to separate your preload script', and globals Buffer/process/setImmediate/clearImmediate; arch 03 §4.2 confirms no auto-downgrade into legacy. Two ownership claims are wrong under the one-owner rule. (1) 'Preload bytes are resolved by the host from the verified app bundle (ExpectedAppIdentity)': keld-pack's ExpectedAppIdentityPayload is the KEL-254 A3 expected-app-identity bytes (app_id, channel, target) that a signed host carries; it is not a per-file verified bundle manifest and verifies no preload bytes. Content authentication lives in the KEL-53/keld-pack canonical archive + update policy path, and no live owner verifies app-bundle file bytes at launch. Naming ExpectedAppIdentity as the verifier creates a phantom owner. (2) 'keld build/keld migrate bundles each preload': both subcommands are KELD-CLI-045 reserved, not live, and the migrate UX is owned by KEL-19 (CLI RFC); A3 must name KEL-19 and the bundler owner rather than assume the facility. decision_packets.decision: On macOS the app preload and the renderer compat runtime run in a content world separate from the KEL-142 bridge world, with their own world-scoped message handler, rather than sharing the bridge world.
facts: FACT (measured, world-probe run by this agent 2026-10-06, macOS 26.5.1, system WKWebView; source and output in scratchpad/prototypes/world-probe): a script placed in the same content world as a bridge-shaped script read the world-scoped handler object directly, posted a forged message that reached the native handler from the main frame, wrapped the global bind hook, captured the host-delivered document nonce, posted a forged invoke carrying the correct nonce, leaked the nonce to the page, and relayed page-chosen bytes to the raw native handler.
FACT (measured, same run): the same script placed in a named content world saw the handler as undefined and the bind hook as undefined, and no forged message reached the native handler.

FACT (measured, same run): a hardened bridge script could freeze its bind hook (the nonce then did not leak), but its attempt to shadow window.webkit threw 'Attempting to change value of a readonly property', so the handler stayed reachable and both forged messages still arrived.
FACT (measured, same run): window.postMessage crosses content worlds, and the handler also exists in subframes of the same world (those messages arrive with isMainFrame false).

FACT: Apple documents that the user content controller defines the handler function 'in all frames in the specified content world' (developer.apple.com, WKUserContentController addScriptMessageHandler(_:contentWorld:name:), JSON endpoint fetched 2026-10-06).

FACT: the live bridge registers its handler in the default client world, assigns the bind and result hooks as plain writable globals, and calls JSON.stringify, Number.isInteger, Array.isArray and Array.from at call time rather than capturing them; the host rejects non-main-frame messages and stale or forged nonces (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs at b4b907c3, read 2026-10-06).

FACT: KEL-142 section 5.1 says the page world must not be able to access the native message-handler object, its handler name, or the host's document binding, and that a page-callable relay 'must accept no broader shape than window.keld.invoke'; AC2 requires the nonce to be absent from page globals and request arguments, and 'Deleting content-world isolation ... must fail a named test' (docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md, read 2026-10-06).

FACT: draw.io's preload calls contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld twice and exposes sendMessage(action, args), which forwards a page-chosen channel to ipcRenderer.send (corpus drawio-desktop @2edf9fb, src/main/electron-preload.js).
FACT: F07-T1 (GitHub #484) lists PANEL-D21 in blocked_by and names a 'KEL-142 spec revision (third world/relay)' as an external predecessor (publish_plan.json).
FACT (Linear, fetched 2026-10-06): KEL-142 Done (completed 2026-10-01), parent KEL-139 Done; KEL-79 Backlog, unassigned. No open Linear issue owns a KEL-142 revision.
inferences: INFERENCE: the world-probe mimics the bridge's two decisive properties (world-scoped handler, writable global bind hook) rather than running the real bridge. The real bridge has the same two properties in code, so the same result is expected.

INFERENCE: arm G as written (adversarial preload must not be able to re-export the handler or nonce) cannot pass in a shared world under any contextBridge value table, because proxying functions is the feature and the handler is reachable by platform design.

INFERENCE: a same-world preload could also alter the trusted script's behaviour by replacing the uncaptured built-ins it calls; host-side validation stays authoritative, but the script would no longer be trusted.

INFERENCE: a DOM postMessage relay from the app world through the bridge world is page-forgeable, so it would let page script send on any granted el: channel even when the preload exposed a narrower API. That is broader than Electron, where the page reaches ipcRenderer only through what the preload exposes, and broader than the section 5.1 relay rule allows.
INFERENCE: relay cost cannot flip the world choice, because the shared world fails a condition the judges called mandatory; cost only informs the relay shape.
unknowns: UNKNOWN: per-call cost of an app-world handler versus a DOM relay. This agent's relay-cost probe produced no result within 120 s in an offscreen web view and the cause was not diagnosed, so the cost is unmeasured.
UNKNOWN: how the app-world handler binds messages to the current document (reusing the host's existing per-document state versus a second nonce).

alternatives.option: A. Separate named app world for preload plus compat runtime, with a second world-scoped handler on the same per-view controller that accepts only compat (el:) envelopes; the KEL-142 handler and nonce stay unreachable by app code.
alternatives.cost: A KEL-142 spec revision (second world and handler), one more host handler path through the existing bridge owner, and an unmeasured per-call cost.
alternatives.new_invariant: App-authored renderer code never shares a content world with the trusted bridge script; the app world's capability is no broader than Electron's ipcRenderer under the window's enumerated el: grant.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142's single-handler assumption; must not become a second transport owner or a second policy check.

alternatives.option: B. Preload in the bridge world, with contextBridge enforcing Electron's value table (maintainer position).
alternatives.cost: Measured: handler and nonce reachable by the preload and re-exportable to the page. KEL-142 AC2 becomes conditional on app code.
alternatives.new_invariant: The app preload is part of the trusted bridge base.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142 section 5.1 and AC2 as written; the 'trusted script' premise.

alternatives.option: C. Separate app world with a nonce-less DOM relay through the bridge world.
alternatives.cost: Page script can forge relay messages, so every granted el: channel becomes page-reachable regardless of what the preload exposes.
alternatives.new_invariant: Page authority equals preload authority for compat channels.
alternatives.invariant_at_risk: KEL-142 section 5.1 relay rule ('no broader shape than window.keld.invoke'); Electron's preload-as-filter contract.

alternatives.option: D. Shared world with a hardened bridge (frozen hooks, hidden handler).
alternatives.cost: Measured: the hook can be frozen but the handler cannot be hidden; it becomes an arms race inside one world.
alternatives.new_invariant: Bridge safety depends on script-level hardening holding against same-world code.

research.summary: [fact] Family = Electron `webviewTag` element: 113 members (65 methods, 35 events, 13 attributes), renderer-only, not exported, carrying Electron's own "we recommend not to use the webview tag" warning. [fact] Corpus demand for the tag itself is zero: draw.io's 7 "webview" hits are six `webviewTag: false` and one `will-attach-webview` → `event.preventDefault()`; Zettlr and electron-quick-start contain no `<webview>`. What the corpus actually needs from this unit is the renderer-side compat user-script: `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` (draw.io 2, Zettlr 5), `ipcRenderer.send/on/once/removeListener/removeAllListeners` (draw.io), `ipcRenderer.invoke` (Zettlr 187 sites) and `sendSync` (Zettlr 6, synchronous `config.get` inside preload-exposed functions), `ipcRenderer.setMaxListeners(100)`, `process.type/versions/platform/env/argv` re-exposed to the page, `webPreferences.additionalArguments` read as `process.argv` in preload, `webUtils.getPathForFile`, and an isolated-world `window.navigation` listener that only works because page code cannot reach preload objects. [fact] Keld live state: macOS-only `window.keld.invoke` installed as a `WKContentWorld.defaultClientWorld` document-start user script plus a frozen pageWorld facade (channel 1 only, 4096 B, one pending invoke, host-minted document nonce, `KELD-WV-011`); WebView2 injects no bridge at all (wry's 96–109 ms blocking injection was deliberately removed); WebKitGTK is wry scaffold with no isolated world; no preload loading, no `@keld/web` package, no renderer `@keld/electron` shim, no custom scheme, no window registry beyond `LifecycleSession` window counting; devtools: WebView2 debug-on/release-off until guard owns `web.devtools`, wry open/close elsewhere. Recommended sequencing: (1) Tier-1 renderer user-script over `window.keld` (requires lifting the KEL-142 floor: multiple pending invokes, string channels, structured-clone codec, host→renderer events) with isolation claimed only on WebKit engines and a documented ▲ page-world emulation on WebView2; (2) `webviewTag:false`/`will-attach-webview` zero-webview semantics as a conformance cell now; (3) `<webview>` → host-owned child webview stays Tier 3 and is not on the draw.io/Zettlr path. Two design atoms need prototypes before any spec: `sendSync` feasibility on system engines (no synchronous native bridge exists on any of the three; only a synchronous XHR to a host scheme could block), and whether WebView2's page-world emulation of `contextBridge` leaks preload internals.

decisions.question: How is `require('electron')` (and Node globals) resolved inside a preload on Keld?
decisions.proposed_answer: Mirror Electron's own sandboxed-preload contract exactly: `keld build`/`keld migrate` bundles each preload (Electron already forbids CommonJS splitting under sandbox) and provides a polyfilled `require` whose loadable map is precisely {contextBridge, crashReporter(map), ipcRenderer, nativeImage(subset), webFrame(subset), webUtils, events, timers, url, node:events, node:timers, node:url} plus globals Buffer, process (synthesized subset), setImmediate/clearImmediate. Preload bytes are resolved by the host from the verified app bundle (ExpectedAppIdentity), never from an app-supplied absolute path; `file:`/`asar:` paths are rewritten at migrate time. Any preload importing outside that map (i.e. relying on sandbox:false / nodeIntegration) is a static-analysis ✘ with an exact diagnostic naming the module; no legacy-profile auto-downgrade.
evidence: sandbox.md: exact module list and 'you will not be able to use CommonJS modules to separate your preload script into multiple files'
process.md: sandboxed process property subset
webview-tag.md: preload 'must be file:' and Node-globals deletion semantics

decisions.alternatives_rejected: Running preload in a Bun role (preload must share the DOM/window with the page — a Bun process has no DOM; would invent a second renderer model). Allowing `require` of arbitrary app files from preload (needs filesystem authority inside the webview principal).
decisions.unknowns: crashReporter and nativeImage subsets available in preload are owned by other units; exact mapping here is only 'present in the loadable map'.

decisions.question: Can ipcRenderer.sendSync keep its blocking caller contract on system engines, and through which lane?
decisions.proposed_answer: [fact] None of WKScriptMessageHandler (async reply), WebView2 postMessage (one-way JSON), or WebKitGTK message handlers block the calling JS. The only engine-neutral primitive that blocks the main thread with a reply is a synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a host-owned scheme/origin (the arch 02 §3 bulk lane). Proposed: sendSync = synchronous XHR POST to `keld://c/el-sync/{channel}` carrying the host-minted document nonce header, host enforces deadline + rate limit, dev build logs a warning per call (KEL-127 wording); response body is the SCV-encoded returnValue. Promise-returning emulation is rejected (changes caller contract; Zettlr's exposed `config.get` must return synchronously). If the prototype shows sync XHR is blocked by CSP/COEP or by engine policy on custom schemes, sendSync becomes a documented ✘ with per-call diagnostics.
evidence: ipc-renderer.md: 'block the whole renderer process until the reply is received'
research 06 bridge table: no binary/sync path; custom scheme streaming on all three (GTK 2.40+)
arch 02 §3: bulk rides keld://c/{channel}; postMessage control-only
briefing KEL-127: sendSync replacement must stay blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned
Zettlr preload: sendSync inside synchronous exposed functions (config.get/set, citation)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Atomics.wait on SharedArrayBuffer (main thread cannot block on Atomics.wait in browsers; requires COOP/COEP and a worker relay). Busy-wait on a flag set by an async reply (freezes the event loop that must deliver the reply — deadlock). Async Promise shim with a quirks flag (violates KEL-127; breaks Zettlr synchronously).
decisions.unknowns: [unknown] Whether WKURLSchemeHandler serves synchronous XHR on the main thread without deadlock when the handler's reply is produced on the host UI thread (WKURLSchemeHandler callbacks arrive on the main thread; a round trip to Bun must not block that thread — KEL-142 §6 rule). [unknown] WebView2 WebResourceRequested deferral semantics under sync XHR. [unknown] Chromium/WebKit timelines for removing synchronous XHR entirely.

decisions.question: What must change in the KEL-142 window.keld floor before an Electron renderer shim can sit on it without a second protocol?
decisions.proposed_answer: Lift, in place, four frozen floor rules via a KEL-142 successor spec (candidate owner KEL-80): (1) pending set > 1 with host-enforced credit (Zettlr fires concurrent invokes from 65 files); (2) string channel names mapped through a host-declared compat namespace (`el:*`, arch 02 §5) onto u16 ids, with undeclared channels failing KELD-WV-011 — the manifest, not the page, declares channels; (3) payload > 4096 B via the bulk lane reference, not a larger inline bound; (4) host→renderer push (`window.keld.on`/EVENT) for ipcRenderer.on and webContents.send. decisions.question: When <webview> ships (Tier 3), is it a host-owned child webview or an iframe emulation, and which attributes map to which Keld owners?
decisions.proposed_answer: Host-owned child webview: a second WebviewId principal created by the host, parented to the embedder's window and positioned from an embedder-reported rect (ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver → host set_bounds), with its own navigation generation, its own preload (same A2/A3 rules), partition→KEL-135 store identity (`persist:`=identity-bound, else memory-only), src/loadURL→host navigate under the KEL-79 navigation allow-list, allowpopups→deny unless granted (KEL-168 handler), useragent→per-view engine UA, nodeintegration/disablewebsecurity/plugins/enable|disableblinkfeatures→never (refused at attach with a code), embedder↔guest ipc (send/sendToHost/ipc-message)→KEL-75 T3 virtual-port pair bound to both generations, executeJavaScript/insertCSS/print/printToPDF/capturePage/openDevTools from the embedder→host-mediated calls evaluated as the embedder principal against explicit grants. getWebContentsId returns a host-minted opaque id. This preserves the 'separate process, asynchronous interaction' semantics Electron documents; an iframe emulation cannot.
